title: Wait, WHEN?!
blurb: Older than you think, newer than you'd guess, and totally out of order.

cards.say: Woolly mammoths [were still alive when the Great Pyramid of Egypt was built], [had tusks that could grow more than 13 feet long], [were still alive when the first Olympic Games were held], and [were close cousins of the elephants living in Asia today].
cards.real: The last mammoths died out on an Arctic island about 4,000 years ago. The first Olympics were in 776 BC, more than 1,000 years later.

cards.say: T. rex [walked the Earth for more than 20 million years], [lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus], [lived at the same time as Triceratops], and [lived when a day on Earth lasted less than 24 hours].
cards.real: T. rex lived from about 67 to 66 million years ago, so roughly one million years, not twenty.

cards.say: Pluto [was discovered after Mickey Mouse's first cartoon came out], [got its name from an 11-year-old girl in England], [was called a planet for only 76 years], and [was discovered before the Wright brothers' first flight].
cards.real: Pluto was found in 1930, 27 years after the Wright brothers first flew in 1903.

cards.say: The Statue of Liberty [is a few years older than the Eiffel Tower in Paris], [stood finished in Paris for ten years before it sailed to America], [opened the same year Coca-Cola was invented], and [worked as a lighthouse for its first 16 years].
cards.real: It was finished in Paris in July 1884 and reached New York in June 1885, packed in 214 crates.

cards.say: Sharks [were swimming in the sea before there were any trees], [have skeletons made of thick, heavy bone], [were around about 200 million years before the first dinosaurs], and [can grow thousands of teeth in one lifetime].
cards.real: Sharks have no bones at all. Their skeletons are made of cartilage, the same bendy stuff that's in your nose and ears.

cards.say: Oreo cookies [went on sale before sliced bread did], [started out as a copy of an older cookie called Hydrox], [are older than the states of Alaska and Hawaii], and [are older than the very first teddy bear].
cards.real: Teddy bears came first, in 1902. The first Oreo was sold ten years later, in March 1912.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook: Alaska and Hawaii both became states in 1959; the first Oreo was sold on March 6, 1912) https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oreo

cards.say: Hot air balloons [carried people for the first time before the Declaration of Independence], [carried a sheep, a duck and a rooster before carrying any people], [were invented by two brothers whose family made paper], and [carried people 120 years before the first airplane flight].
cards.real: The first people flew in a balloon over Paris on November 21, 1783, seven years after the Declaration of Independence in 1776.

cards.say: The Moon [had people walk on it before the first home video game console was sold], [had its last Apollo moonwalk before the first Star Wars movie], [has a dark side that never gets any sunlight], and [has two golf balls lying on it that were hit in 1971].
cards.real: The far side gets just as much sunlight as the side we see. We just never see it, because the same side of the Moon always faces Earth.

cards.say: Nintendo [is older than the game of basketball], [ran its own taxi company back in the 1960s], [is older than the very first Ferris wheel], and [stopped making playing cards once it started making video games].
cards.real: Nintendo never stopped. It started out making playing cards in 1889 and still makes card games today.

cards.say: Barbie [had her own spacesuit four years before anyone walked on the Moon], [cost 30 dollars when she first went on sale], [has the full name Barbara Millicent Roberts], and [is older than the first trip to space by a person].
cards.real: The first Barbie, in 1959, cost just 3 dollars.

cards.say: LEGO [started out making wooden toys in 1932], [made its first plastic bricks after World War II ended], [gets its name from the Danish word for brick], and [sold plastic bricks before Disneyland opened].
cards.real: LEGO comes from the Danish words leg godt, which mean play well.

cards.say: The Great Wall of China [can be seen from the Moon with just your eyes], [was started before the Roman Empire began], [has sticky rice in the mortar between its bricks], and [was still being built after Columbus reached America].
cards.real: It's far too narrow to see from the Moon with just your eyes. That story is a myth.
